newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary unveils 300 bln forint road expansion plan.
newsitem.headline: Hungary unveils 300 bln forint road expansion plan.

text.p: Hungary said on Thursday it plans to spend 300 billion forints ($1.7 billion) on major highways through the year 2004 and would curb the use of private concessionary companies to build them.

The package, announced by government spokesman Elemer Kiss after the weekly cabinet meeting, calls for improvements to five major roads, including the M5 to the border with former Yugoslavia and the M3 in north-central Hungary, near Eger.
Kiss said that based on 1997 prices, Hungary expected to spend about 300 billion forints, including 37 billion for technical work and preparation and 240 billion on actual construction.

He said the government would examine several financing methods, including the central budget and a road fund, but planned to cut back on the use of private concessions, whose toll charges have sparked widespread criticism from motorists and local municipalities.
"There will be several sources of financing in future, so we can assume that...exclusive concession-based construction will not happen," Kiss said.

"Of course it is not impossible that we will have that as well as a partial financing solution, but considering that that is the most costly solution, there is this change in philosophy from the previous government," he said.

Last month the government authorised the Ministry of Transport to start talks on reducing controversial tolls on motorways operated by the concessionary companies, which introduced tolls in Hungary for the first time a year ago.

An 850 forints ($4.85) fee for a 56-km stretch of the motorway south from Budapest has provoked protests from Hungarian motorists while mayors of villages on the road parallel to the highway complained of increased traffic.
